title: Elastic Net Regression Quiz
description: Test your understanding of elastic net regression

questions.question: What does the l1_ratio parameter control in Elastic Net regression?
options: The overall regularization strength
The balance between L1 and L2 regularization
The learning rate for gradient descent
The number of features to select
questions.explanation: The l1_ratio parameter controls the balance between L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) regularization. When l1_ratio = 0, it's pure Ridge; when l1_ratio = 1, it's pure Lasso.

questions.question: If l1_ratio = 0.7 in Elastic Net, what does this mean?
options: 70% Ridge regularization, 30% Lasso regularization
70% Lasso regularization, 30% Ridge regularization
The model will select exactly 70% of features
The regularization strength is set to 0.7
questions.explanation: l1_ratio = 0.7 means 70% of the regularization penalty comes from L1 (Lasso) and 30% from L2 (Ridge). Higher l1_ratio values favor feature selection.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of Elastic Net over pure Lasso regression?
options: It's always faster to compute
It provides more stable feature selection with correlated features
It never sets coefficients to zero
It doesn't require hyperparameter tuning
questions.explanation: Elastic Net provides more stable feature selection than pure Lasso, especially when features are correlated. The L2 component helps maintain stability while the L1 component still allows feature selection.

questions.question: In the Elastic Net penalty term α × [l1_ratio × L1 + (1 - l1_ratio) × L2], what happens when α increases?
options: Only L1 regularization increases
Only L2 regularization increases
Both L1 and L2 regularization increase proportionally
The balance between L1 and L2 changes
questions.explanation: When α (alpha) increases, both L1 and L2 regularization components increase proportionally. Alpha controls the overall regularization strength, while l1_ratio controls the balance between them.

questions.question: Which scenario is Elastic Net particularly well-suited for?
options: Small datasets with few features
High-dimensional data with correlated feature groups
Time series data with temporal dependencies
Binary classification problems only
questions.explanation: Elastic Net excels with high-dimensional data containing correlated feature groups. It can perform feature selection while handling correlation better than pure Lasso.

questions.question: What is the soft thresholding function used for in Elastic Net?
options: To implement the L2 regularization component
To implement the L1 regularization component
To normalize the input features
To compute the final predictions
questions.explanation: Soft thresholding implements the L1 regularization component. It can set coefficients to exactly zero when they fall below the threshold, enabling feature selection.

questions.question: If you want Elastic Net to behave exactly like Ridge regression, what should you set l1_ratio to?
options: It's impossible to make Elastic Net behave like Ridge
questions.explanation: Setting l1_ratio = 0.0 makes Elastic Net behave exactly like Ridge regression, as it eliminates the L1 penalty term and uses only L2 regularization.

questions.question: Why is feature normalization particularly important for Elastic Net regression?
options: It makes the algorithm run faster
Regularization penalties are sensitive to feature scales
It's required for the soft thresholding function to work
It prevents overfitting automatically
questions.explanation: Feature normalization is crucial because regularization penalties (both L1 and L2) are sensitive to the scale of features. Without normalization, features with larger scales would be penalized more heavily.
